visual_description: The image displays a logo for the "Healthy Brain Initiative" with the subtitle "Road Map for Indian Country." On the left side is a stylized blue brain icon composed of geometric shapes. The text "HEALTHY BRAIN" appears in large, bold, dark blue capital letters on the top line, with "INITIATIVE" directly below it in slightly smaller but still bold capital letters. Beneath that, the phrase "Road Map for Indian Country" is written in a lighter blue, sentence-case font. The entire composition uses shades of blue against a white background.

The image displays the logo of the National Council of Urban Indian Health. The design features a circular emblem with stylized blue silhouettes representing people and urban structures, including buildings and a bridge. Text encircles the central graphic, reading "NATIONAL COUNCIL OF URBAN INDIAN HEALTH" in capital letters.

plain_text:
Educate and Empower Community Members Strategies
Benefit(s) for Each StrategyLow DifficultyModerate DifficultyGreater DifficultyLife Course
2. Encourage community members to use effective interventions, best practices, and traditional wellness practices to protect brain health, address cognitive impairment, and support persons living with dementia and their caregivers.
Well-designed programs have been shown to benefit persons living with dementia and caregivers. These programs should be readily accessible to all in need. Access to these programs and tools is particularly crucial for people living with dementia who live alone.• Promote healthy aging during traditional wellness events, calling attention to the benefits of cognition that these activities provide• Provide a space for caregivers to network, provide support to each other and discuss their best practices• Create a healthy aging campaign in your community• Educate I/T/U health staff on risk and protective factors and give them the tools they need to inform patients on how their behaviors/lifestyle could impact them later in life
• Provide information on support services in your community (transportation, legal and financial assistance, training for community members working with older adults, peer support groups)• Modify existing programs or interventions, such as the Special Diabetes Program for Indians, to include information on healthy aging and Alzheimer's• Develop an app or other message delivery mechanisms to share tips and ways to live a healthy cognitive life
• Add resources to your webpage (see list of resources on page 13)• Identify champions among the community to help spread the message on healthy aging. This can be a Tribal or community leader, a traditional healer, or youth
• Programs and practices to keep those living with dementia connected to their community• Adapt community events to encourage participation by people living with dementia and their caregivers (such as having a quiet space, adapting event roles so they can readily participate if they choose)
• Legal and financial assistance
• Training for all community members working with older adults
• Long-term care for those whose families live far away
